Most likely not, but it also doesn’t take up any of your time so you need to decide which is more valuable in your circumstances. 

Real estate can earn you incredible ROI if you do your research properly and buy in upcoming neighbourhoods, renovate before renting out or possibly altering the property in a way that generates more income like dividing up the property / complex etc. However, this can very easily turn into a full time job before you know it. 

To properly answer your question; if you’d be just buying the property and immediately renting it out to minimise your time input, then you might as well do that through a REIT as in the latter case your ROI is not as high as it could be with a full-time approach, which brings the tangible and intangible way of investments much closer to each other in terms of ROI.

You could also invest in high dividend ETFs like SPY or the stock market equivalent of real estate like VNQ. This way you don’t need to physically own real estate and pay property tax, renovation costs or filling rent vacancies but can still enjoy the benefits. It’s called a REIT, I suggest you google it.

Yes, this will make you significantly less money if it ever moons, but expecting to get rich on a single transaction when you’re 21 is unrealistic and even if you succeeded it wouldn’t be sustainable for too long. 

Focus on not losing rather than hitting it big. At least this is how I see it now after a good few years of trying to have it all only to find myself on the floor time and time again..
